title: Quarterly Sprint Bridge — Hosted API & Model Catalog Alignment
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a sprint-to-quarter playbook (the 'Sprint Bridge') that operationalizes the Q2 roadmap for Hosted API and the Model Catalog. The playbook will translate strategic quarterly milestones into sprint-level deliverables across PM, Eng, Design, and Applied ML, define gating criteria for model onboarding and hosted deployments, and establish metrics and cadence for OKR tracking and rollback/fallback policy triggers.
goals: Define sprint-level deliverables that map to the top 6 Q2 roadmap milestones for Hosted API and Model Catalog
Create a reusable gating matrix for model onboarding (quality, latency, cost) and regional rollout readiness
Embed eval-driven acceptance criteria into release gates to reduce post-deploy regressions by 50%
Set a cross-team cadence (weekly sync + biweekly roadmap review) and dashboard slices for OKR health
milestones: M1: Draft Sprint Bridge playbook and gating matrix — 2026-03-18
M2: Prototype automated eval checks integrated with CI for model snapshots — 2026-03-31
M3: First sprint plan aligned to playbook published to teams + kickoff — 2026-04-01
M4: Dashboard & alert set for OKR/metric drift and rollback triggers — 2026-04-10
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc reviewed and approved by Eng, Design, Applied ML, and SRE
Gating matrix implemented as a checklist template in Confluence and paired GitHub PR checklist
Two model onboarding CVs pass automated eval checks in CI along with performance regression thresholds
OKR dashboard shows expected metrics for the first sprint and emits an alert on deviation >20%
dependencies: ENG-4021 (runtime: CI hooks for model snapshots)
DES-221 (UX: rollout modal and dashboard widgets)
risks: Incomplete CI eval coverage may allow regressions to reach staging
Regional capacity constraints could block rollout windows despite readiness
Misalignment on quality thresholds between Applied ML and Product could delay onboarding
Dashboard instrumentation gaps may hide early OKR drift
decisions: Adopt an eval-first gating approach: model PRs must pass defined eval suite before canary
Use the existing hosted API canary path as the default rollback mechanism for model-level regressions
Prioritize EU region for early Q2 rollouts due to enterprise demand and data residency requirements
notes: This Sprint Bridge is intended to be lightweight and iterated weekly. Focus on high-leverage automation (CI evals, checklist templates) and one clear regional pilot. Avoid creating heavyweight process overhead — the goal is to reduce rework and speed up safe rollouts.
